question: What is this AI Accelerator circle at DATEV, and is Christopher leading it?
expected: Explains that the AI Accelerator circle is an informal internal DATEV group that exchanges on AI adoption in the company, and that Christopher is a member. It does not claim he leads it.
key_facts: internal AI Accelerator circle at DATEV
informal group exchanging on AI adoption
Christopher is a member, not the leader

question: How widely is the Shared Knowledge Hub used today, and how far is it supposed to grow?
expected: States that the hub is used in 10 projects today and that a rollout to about 30 projects is planned. It does not present the 30 as already reached.

question: So Christopher is the project lead of the knowledge hub and manages the people on it?
expected: Corrects the premise. He co-leads the team-internal hub project together with a colleague, not alone, and the profile lists no people-management or team-lead role.

question: Technically, how does the search in his knowledge hub work?
expected: Describes the hybrid search. A BM25 keyword search with stemming for German and English and a semantic search over embeddings run in parallel, and the results are merged by rank fusion (RRF). It adds no invented components.
key_facts: BM25 keyword search with German and English stemming

question: Are the hub's search functions exposed to the agents as MCP tools?
expected: Explains that agents reach the hub through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), but that the hybrid search runs through Programmatic Tool Calling, not as MCP tools.
key_facts: agents reach the hub via MCP
hybrid search runs through Programmatic Tool Calling

question: Which vector database did he move the knowledge hub to in September 2026?
expected: Corrects the premise. In 09/2026 the hub moved to a database behind the MCP, but that database does no vector search, and the embeddings are stored separately. It does not name a vector DB product or claim vector-database expertise.
key_facts: 09/2026 moved to a database behind the MCP
the database does no vector search

question: Did the knowledge hub save any tokens? Give me the exact figure and the reason.
expected: States that an analysis showed 30 to 40 % fewer tokens, because agents only get the context their task needs. It does not give a single inflated number.
key_facts: agents only get the context their task needs

question: How does the hub decide which entries come first in the results?
expected: Explains that a named ID ranks first, that linked entries of the best hits are added, and that outdated or closed entries count less.
key_facts: linked entries of the best hits are added
outdated or closed entries count less

question: Which AI assistant helps him write the Crossplane provider, and is it the same tool he uses for AgentBrain?
expected: Says the Crossplane provider is written in Go with GitHub Copilot at work. AgentBrain is a private project built on Claude Code, which is not used at DATEV, so they are different tools.
key_facts: Crossplane provider: Go with GitHub Copilot
Claude Code is not used at DATEV

question: How did the idea for the Shared Knowledge Hub come about, and what problem does it solve for coding agents?
expected: States that the hub came out of daily work with agentic development, among others on the Crossplane provider. It is a shared context store, so context stays available across sessions, tools and repositories.
key_facts: came out of daily agentic development work
among others on the Crossplane provider
shared context store for AI coding agents
context available across sessions, tools and repositories

question: Which came first, the knowledge hub or AgentBrain, and how many specialist agents does AgentBrain have?
expected: States that the hub started first (since 07/2026) and AgentBrain later (since 10/2026). AgentBrain has a manager agent and ten specialist agents.
key_facts: manager agent plus ten specialist agents

question: Does AgentBrain run completely on local models?
expected: Says no. The agents use cloud models, and only the vault search runs locally. It does not claim a fully local setup.
key_facts: only the vault search runs locally

question: Which LLM did he run in the Kafka agent proof of concept, and what served it?
expected: Names the model qwen3:4b-instruct-2507, running locally on Ollama on his laptop. It does not name another model or invent a cloud setup.

question: What Kafka version and cluster setup does the LLM proof of concept use?
expected: States that the PoC runs Kafka 4.3.2 with Strimzi on kind, locally with fake data.

question: How did he make sure the Kafka agent can't change anything in the cluster?
expected: Explains that the agent has five read-only tools over MCP and that read-only is enforced in three layers: a tool allow-list, a Kafka user with only Describe and Read rights, and the authorizer.
key_facts: Kafka user with only Describe and Read rights

question: Did he ever test what happens if the agent tries to delete a topic? What was the outcome?
expected: Describes the negative test. With the tool filter turned off on purpose, the agent was asked to delete a topic; Kafka refused all 5 attempts and the topic was still there.

question: What were the median time-to-first-token values in his load test at 1, 10 and 20 users?
expected: Gives about 0.6 s, 6.4 s and 14.1 s for 1, 10 and 20 concurrent users. It may add that speed stayed at about 40 tokens per second per user and that no request failed.

question: Given his Kafka LLM project, it's fair to say he has MLOps experience with training, fine-tuning and a model registry, right?
expected: Corrects the premise. The profile lists no MLOps experience; the PoC covers only local serving, monitoring and a load test on his laptop with fake data. It has no model training, fine-tuning, model registry, ML pipelines or drift monitoring, and makes no production claim.
key_facts: PoC covers local serving, monitoring and load test
no training, fine-tuning, model registry, ML pipelines or drift monitoring
local on laptop with fake data, no production claim

question: How many Claude Academy certificates does he have, when did he get them, and are they professional certifications?
expected: States six Claude Academy certificates from Anthropic, all issued 11/2026. They are online course certificates, not professional certifications.

question: Seit wann leitet Christopher den Shared Knowledge Hub, und macht er das allein?
expected: Antwortet auf Deutsch: Das Projekt läuft seit 07/2026, und Christopher leitet es gemeinsam mit einem Kollegen, nicht allein.

question: Wurde der Hub im September 2026 auf eine Vektordatenbank umgestellt?
expected: Antwortet auf Deutsch und korrigiert die Annahme: Im 09/2026 zog der Hub auf eine Datenbank hinter dem MCP. Diese Datenbank macht keine Vektorsuche, und die Embeddings werden getrennt davon gespeichert.

question: Mit wie vielen Fragen hat er die Suche in AgentBrain getestet, und wie viel günstiger war sie?
expected: Antwortet auf Deutsch: In seinem eigenen Test mit 187 Fragen war die lokale Suche 49 % günstiger als seine vorherige Suche, bei gleicher Antwortqualität.

question: Worauf basiert AgentBrain, und ist das ein Projekt bei DATEV?
expected: Antwortet auf Deutsch: AgentBrain ist ein privates Projekt, ein Multi-Agenten-System auf Basis von Claude Code mit einem Obsidian-Vault. Es ist nicht Teil seiner Arbeit bei DATEV, wo er GitHub Copilot nutzt.
key_facts: nicht Teil der Arbeit bei DATEV

question: Wie viele Personen schult er in KI-Werkzeugen, und wer sind diese Personen?
expected: Antwortet auf Deutsch: Er schult gemeinsam mit einem Kollegen sein eigenes Team von 15 Personen in KI-Werkzeugen.

question: Auf welcher Grafikkarte läuft das lokale Modell im Kafka-PoC, und wie schnell ist es pro Nutzer?
expected: Antwortet auf Deutsch: Das Modell läuft lokal auf Ollama auf einer GTX 1060 mit 6 GB. Die Geschwindigkeit blieb bei etwa 40 Tokens pro Sekunde pro Nutzer.
key_facts: etwa 40 Tokens pro Sekunde pro Nutzer
